rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking desire as a god means obeying it and making it the basis of one's religion, without hearing proof or seeing evidence.
rows.anchor: بأن أطاعه وبنى عليه دينه لا يسمع حجة ولا يبصر دليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second object is advanced for emphasis.
rows.anchor: وإنما قدم المفعول الثاني للعناية به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first question expresses confirmation and astonishment; the second denies that the Prophet could guard such a person from idolatry and sin.
rows.anchor: فالاستفهام الأول للتقرير والتعجيب والثاني للإنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Am means rather: should you think most of them hear or reason, so that signs and arguments might benefit them and you hope for their faith?
rows.anchor: بل أتحسب. { أن أكثرهم يسمعون أو يعقلون } فتجدي لهم الآيات أو الحجج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a stronger reproach than the preceding one, warranting a shift to it.
rows.anchor: وهو أشد مذمة مما قبله حتى حق بالإضراب عنه إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most is specified because some believed or recognized the truth but resisted from arrogance or fear of losing leadership.
rows.anchor: وتخصيص الأكثر لأنه كان منهم من آمن ومنهم من عقل الحق وكابر استكبارا وخوفا على الرئاسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They resemble cattle because they do not benefit when signs strike their ears and do not reflect on proofs and miracles they witness.
rows.anchor: في عدم انتفاعهم بقرع الآيات آذانهم وعدم تدبرهم فيما شاهدوا من الدلائل والمعجزات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cattle follow their caretakers, distinguish kindness from harm, seek benefits, and avoid harms; these people do none of that toward their Lord.
rows.anchor: لأنها تنقاد لمن يتعهدها وتميز من يحسن إليها ممن يسيء إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People fail to recognize their Lord's beneficence versus Satan's harm, seek no supreme reward, and do not guard against the worst harm, punishment.
rows.anchor: ولا يعرفون إحسانه من إساءة الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike people, cattle that neither believe truth nor do good also do not believe falsehood or commit evil.
rows.anchor: ولأنها إن لم تعتقد حقا ولم تكتسب خيرا لم تعتقد باطلا ولم تكتسب شرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Animal ignorance harms no one, whereas human ignorance produces strife and turns people away from truth.
rows.anchor: ولأن جهالتها لا تضر بأحد وجهالة هؤلاء تؤدي إلى هيج الفتن وصد الناس عن الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cattle cannot seek perfection and so are not blameworthy; people can, and their failure merits the severest punishment.
rows.anchor: ولأنها غير متمكنة من طلب الكمال فلا تقصير منها ولا ذم وهؤلاء مقصرون ومستحقون أعظم العقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rely on the Everliving to ward off opponents' harm and dispense with their recompense; only He deserves reliance, since mortal protectors perish and leave reliance futile.
rows.anchor: في استكفاء شرورهم والإغناء عن أجورهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Glorify God by declaring Him free of deficiencies while praising His perfections, and seek further favor through gratitude for His abundant blessings.
rows.anchor: ونزهه عن صفات النقصان مثنيا عليه بأوصاف الكمال طالبا لمزيد الأنعام بالشكر على سوابغه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows what His servants do, hidden and manifest, so their belief or disbelief need not trouble the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ما ظهر منها وما بطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning creation and the throne further establishes God's right to be relied on as creator and governor of all.
rows.anchor: زيادة تقرير لكونه حقيقا بأن يتوكل عليه من حيث إنه الخالق للكل والمتصرف فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gradual creation encourages steadfastness and patience: despite complete power, God created things deliberately and by stages.
rows.anchor: فإنه تعالى مع كمال قدرته وسرعة نفاذ أمره في كل مراد خلق الأشياء على تؤدة وتدرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rahman may be the predicate of the relative pronoun, an omitted predicate if it modifies al-Hayy, or a substitute for the hidden subject of istawa; it is also read genitive as an attribute of al-Hayy.
rows.anchor: و { الرحمن } خبر للذي إن جعلته مبتدأ ولمحذوف إن جعلته صفة للحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ask God, Gabriel, or someone who knows earlier scriptures about the creation and istiwa; another view refers the pronoun to al-Rahman and directs questioners to knowledgeable People of the Book if they reject that name for God.
rows.anchor: فاسأل عما ذكر من الخلق والاستواء عالما يخبرك بحقيقته وهو الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the alternate reading, al-Rahman can begin the sentence and the following words be its predicate; the name's equivalent occurs in earlier scriptures.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا يجوز أن يكون { الرحمن } مبتدأ والخبر ما بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question takes عن when it implies searching, takes ب when it implies attention, and may also attach خبيرا as a complement.
rows.anchor: والسؤال كما يعدى بعن لتضمنه معنى التفتيش يعدى بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They either did not use al-Rahman as a name for God or thought the command referred to someone else.
rows.anchor: لأنهم ما كانوا يطلقونه على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their question can mean prostrating to the one commanded, or to your command without knowing its basis.
rows.anchor: أي للذي تأمرناه يعني تأمرنا بسجوده أو لأمرك لنا من غير عرفان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative explanation is that the name al-Rahman was foreignized and unfamiliar to them.
rows.anchor: وقيل لأنه كان معربا لم يسمعوه

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: They read يأمرنا with yāʾ, making the words the speech of some of them to one another.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي «يأمرنا» بالياء على أنه قول بعضهم لبعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to prostrate to al-Rahman increased their aversion to faith.
rows.anchor: { وزادهم } أي الأمر بالسجود { للرحمن }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavenly mansions are the twelve zodiac signs; they are named after lofty palaces and are stations for the wandering planets, as dwellings are for inhabitants.
rows.anchor: يعني البروج الاثني عشر سميت به وهي القصور العالية لأنها للكواكب السيارة كالمنازل لسكانها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word buruj derives from tabarruj because the mansions are conspicuous.
rows.anchor: واشتقاقه من التبرج لظهوره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lamp is the sun, supported by the verse about God making the sun a lamp.
rows.anchor: يعني الشمس لقوله وجعل الشمس سراجا

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: They read سرجا, referring to the sun and the large stars.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي «سرجا» وهي الشمس والكواكب الكبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon is bright at night; an alternate vocalization can mean possessing a moon, a plural of قمراء, or can be synonymous with moon, like the cited paired forms.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { وقمرا } أي ذا قمر وهو جمع قمراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رسول is singular because it is a verbal noun used adjectivally and can denote either the envoy or the message.
rows.anchor: أفرد الرسول لأنه مصدر وصف به فإنه مشترك بين المرسل والرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited anonymous poetic line attests رسول as the word that can express the message sent.
rows.anchor: لقد كذب الواشون ما فهت عندهم بسر ولا أرسلتهم برسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dual and singular forms are both used because Moses and Aaron are brothers, because sender or message is one, or because each means himself individually.
rows.anchor: ولذلك ثنى تارة وأفرد أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to send Bani Israel follows from رسول implying sending, which itself implies speaking; it means let them go with us to Syria.
rows.anchor: أي أرسل لتضمن الرسول معنى الإرسال المتضمن معنى القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh addressed Moses after the two came and delivered their message; in our midst means in our houses.
rows.anchor: أي فرعون لموسى بعد ما أتياه فقالا له ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A walid is a child, named for being near birth.
rows.anchor: طفلا سمي به لقربه من الولادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed report says Moses stayed among them thirty years, spent ten in Midian, returned to call them to God for thirty years, and remained fifty after the drowning.
rows.anchor: قيل لبث فيهم ثلاثين سنة ثم خرج إلى مدين عشر سنين ثم عاد إليهم يدعوهم إلى الله ثلاثين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh reproaches Moses for killing the Copt, magnifying the deed after listing the favor he claims to have shown him.
rows.anchor: يعني قتل القبطي، وبخه به معظما إياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternate reading with kasra in فعلتك treats the deed as a single killing by a blow.
rows.anchor: فعلتك بالكسر لأنها كانت قتلة بالوكز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: You are ungrateful to my favor because you killed my close associates; alternatively, you are among those now rejecting my favor, with the phrase construed as a circumstantial clause.
rows.anchor: بنعمتي حتى عمدت إلى قتل خواصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Pharaoh makes an independent judgment that Moses disbelieves in his divinity or favor because of his opposition, or belongs to those who disbelieved in their religion.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون حكما مبتدأ عليه بأنه من الكافرين بآلهيته أو بنعمته لما عاد عليه بالمخالفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الضالين can mean the ignorant, as an alternate reading explicitly uses جاهلين; it can also mean someone acting as the ignorant and foolish do.
rows.anchor: من الجاهلين وقد قرىء به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that Moses was mistaken, since he did not intend to kill him.
rows.anchor: أو من الخاطئين لأنه لم يتعمد قتله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, he did not foresee what the blow would cause, since he intended only to discipline him.
rows.anchor: أو من الذاهلين عما يؤول إليه الوكز لأنه أراد به التأديب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may also mean forgetful, as in the verse about one woman forgetting.
rows.anchor: أو الناسين من قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses fled from them out of fear; God then gave him wisdom and made him a messenger.
rows.anchor: ففررت منكم لما خفتكم فوهب لي ربي حكما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning his wisdom and messengership first answers Pharaoh's attempt to discredit his prophethood through the killing.
rows.anchor: رد أولا بذلك ما وبخه به قدحا في نبوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses does not explicitly deny the upbringing because it is true and does not disprove his claim; he shows it was actually a calamity caused by Israelite enslavement.
rows.anchor: ولم يصرح برده لأنه كان صدقا غير قادح في دعواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The upbringing Pharaoh calls a favor was outwardly so, but in fact Moses' arrival and rearing in Pharaoh's home resulted from enslaving Israel and killing their sons.
rows.anchor: أي وتلك التربية نعمة تمنها علي ظاهرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative supplies a rhetorical hamza of denial: is this a favor you claim while enslaving Israel? The clause can be parsed as predicate, apposition, genitive with omitted باء, or accusative with it omitted.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنه مقدر بهمزة الإنكار أي تلك نعمة تمنها علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes that as an allusion to a heinous trait, with enslavement of Israel explaining the claimed favor.
rows.anchor: وقيل تلك إشارة إلى خصلة شنعاء مبهمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular you is used for the favor because Pharaoh alone imposed it, while Moses feared and fled from Pharaoh and his courtiers.
rows.anchor: وإنما وحد الخطاب في تمنها وجمع فيما قبله لأن المنة كانت منه وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Moses' answer did not make Pharaoh retreat, Pharaoh challenged his claim by asking about the sender's nature.
rows.anchor: لما سمع جواب ما طعن به فيه ورأى أنه لم يرعو بذلك شرع في الاعتراض على دعواه فبدأ بالاستفسار عن حقيقة المرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses describes God through the clearest attributes and effects because individuals can only be defined through properties and actions.
rows.anchor: عرفه بأظهر خواصه وآثاره لما امتنع تعريف الأفراد إلا بذكر الخواص والأفعال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they are certain, they know sensible bodies are contingent because of their composition, multiplicity, and changing states, so they require a necessary origin.
rows.anchor: إن كنتم موقنين الأشياء محققين لها علمتم أن هذه الأجرام المحسوسة ممكنة لتركبها وتعددها وتغير أحوالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That necessary origin must originate all contingent things, whether perceptible or not; otherwise there would be multiple necessary beings or contingent things independent of it, both impossible.
rows.anchor: وذلك المبدىء لا بد وأن يكون مبدأ لسائر الممكنات ما يمكن أن يحس بها وما لا يمكن وإلا لزم تعدد الواجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The necessary being is defined only by external concomitants, since defining it through itself or an intrinsic component would imply composition.
rows.anchor: لا يمكن تعريفه إلا بلوازمه الخارجية لامتناع التعريف بنفسه وبما هو داخل فيه لاستحالة التركيب في ذاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh asks his circle to listen because Moses answers a question about God's nature by describing His acts; alternatively, Pharaoh claims the heavens are self-moving or their dependence on a cause is unknown.
rows.anchor: جوابه سألته عن حقيقته وهو يذكر أفعاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses shifts to their Lord and their first forefathers' Lord, where a similar claim is harder to imagine and dependence on a wise maker is clearer and nearer to observation.
rows.anchor: عدولا إلى ما لا يمكن أن يتوهم فيه مثله ويشك في افتقاره إلى مصور حكيم ويكون أقرب إلى الناظر وأوضح عند التأمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh calls Moses' answer mad because it responds to another question, and calls him your messenger sarcastically.
rows.anchor: أسأله عن شيء ويجيبني عن آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses points to the sun's daily movement from east to west along a changing course, which usefully orders the affairs of creation.
rows.anchor: تشاهدون كل يوم أنه يأتي بالشمس من المشرق ويحركها على مدار غير مدار اليوم الذي قبله حتى يبلغها إلى المغرب على وجه نافع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they reason, they will know there is no stronger answer; Moses first spoke gently, then met their greater hostility with firmness.
rows.anchor: إن كان لكم عقل علمتم أن لا جواب لكم فوق ذلك لاينهم أولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After losing the argument, Pharaoh turns from debate to a threat, as obstinate people do when defeated.
rows.anchor: عدولا إلى التهديد عن المحاجة بعد الانقطاع وهكذا ديدن المعاند المحجوج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's threat is evidence that he claimed divinity and denied a creator; his scoffing at Moses' answer responds to attributing lordship to another.
rows.anchor: واستدل به على ادعائه الألوهية وإنكاره الصانع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Perhaps Pharaoh was a materialist who thought control of a region through power or a favorable star entitled its ruler to worship.
rows.anchor: ولعله كان دهريا اعتقد أن من ملك قطرا أو تولى أمره بقوة طالعه استحق العبادة من أهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in المسجونين refers to prisoners whose fate was known: Pharaoh confined them in a deep pit until death, making the threat stronger than saying he would imprison Moses.
rows.anchor: اللام في { المسجونين } للعهد أي ممن عرفت حالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Azlafna means We brought near; the others are Pharaoh and his people, who entered on the Israelites' trail into their passage.
rows.anchor: وقربنا. { ثم الآخرين } فرعون وقومه حتى دخلوا على أثرهم مداخلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses and all his companions were saved because the sea was preserved in its parted state until they crossed.
rows.anchor: بحفظ البحر على تلك الهيئة إلى أن عبروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The others drowned when the sea closed over them.
rows.anchor: بإطباقه عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The event was an extraordinary sign; God is mighty in taking vengeance on His enemies and merciful to His allies.
rows.anchor: المنتقم من أعدائه. { الرحيم } بأوليائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people did not take heed: no surviving Egyptian believed, and Israel later asked for a cow to worship, made the calf, and demanded to see God.
rows.anchor: إذ لم يؤمن بها أحد ممن بقي في مصر من القبط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to recite Abraham's story to the Arab polytheists.
rows.anchor: { واتل عليهم } على مشركي العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham asks his father and people what they worship to show that their objects do not deserve worship.
rows.anchor: سألهم ليريهم أن ما يعبدونه لا يستحق العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They boastfully elaborate that they worship idols and remain devoted to them;ظل here means continue, though another view limits their worship to daytime.
rows.anchor: و «نظل» ها هنا بمعنى ندوم. وقيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks whether idols hear their prayer, or whether they hear them praying, with the omitted wording inferred from context.
rows.anchor: أيسمعون دعاءكم أو يسمعونكم تدعون فحذف ذلك لدلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading means do they hear your answer to the prayer; the present tense with إذ vividly reenacts the past scene.
rows.anchor: أي يسمعونكم الجواب عن دعائكم ومجيئه مضارعا مع { إذ } على حكاية الحال الماضية استحضارا لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham asks whether the idols benefit their worship or harm those who abandon them.
rows.anchor: على عبادتكم لها. { أو يضرون } من أعرض عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people stop claiming the idols hear or affect them and retreat to imitation of their forefathers.
rows.anchor: أضربوا عن أن يكون لهم سمع أو يتوقع منهم ضر أو نفع، والتجأوا إلى التقليد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ancient practice does not establish correctness, and falsehood does not become truth through age.
rows.anchor: فإن التقدم لا يدل على الصحة ولا ينقلب به الباطل حقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols are enemies to their worshippers because their worship harms them more than a human enemy would; alternatively, Satan, who tempts them to worship idols, is their greatest enemy.
rows.anchor: يريد أنهم أعداء لعابديهم من حيث إنهم يتضررون من جهتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham presents this as advice to himself indirectly, which is more persuasive than direct accusation and signals that he begins with himself to invite acceptance.
rows.anchor: لكنه صور الأمر في نفسه تعريضا لهم فإنه أنفع في النصح من التصريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular word enemy is used because it is originally a verbal noun or a relational adjective.
rows.anchor: وإفراد العدو لأنه في الأصل مصدر أو بمعنى النسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception of the Lord of the worlds may be disconnected, or connected if the pronoun refers to every object worshipped, since some forebears worshipped God.
rows.anchor: استثناء منقطع أو متصل على أن الضمير لكل معبود عبدوه وكان من آبائهم من عبد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guides every creature to the purpose for which it was created in worldly and afterlife affairs, as in the verse about the One who determined and guided.
rows.anchor: لأنه يهدي كل مخلوق لما خلق له من أمور المعاش والمعاد كما قال تعالى والذى قدر فهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance develops from creation to life's end, enabling benefits and warding off harms; for humans it begins with the fetus drawing menstrual blood in the womb and ends in guidance to Paradise.
rows.anchor: هداية مدرجة من مبدأ إيجاده إلى منتهى أجله يتمكن بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ف in فهو is causal if the relative clause is the predicate, but conjunctive if it modifies Lord of the worlds, since creation is completed while guidance continues.
rows.anchor: والفاء للسببية إن جعل الموصول مبتدأ وللعطف إن جعل صفة رب العالمين فيكون اختلاف النظم لتقدم الخلق واستمرار الهداية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first syntactic analysis, the relative clause about feeding is a subject with an omitted predicate understood from what precedes, as are the two clauses after it.
rows.anchor: على الأول مبتدأ محذوف الخبر لدلالة ما قبله عليه وكذا اللذان بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the relative pronoun in either syntactic analysis shows that each described act independently warrants the judgment about God.
rows.anchor: وتكرير الموصول على الوجهين للدلالة على أن كل واحدة من الصلات مستقلة باقتضاء الحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Healing is joined to feeding and drinking because health and illness usually follow from what one eats and drinks.
rows.anchor: عطف على { يطعمني ويسقين } لأنه من روادفهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Illness is not attributed to God because the passage enumerates favors; death can be attributed to Him since death itself is not harmful, whereas its precursors are.
rows.anchor: وإنما لم ينسب المرض إليه تعالى لأن المقصود تعديد النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For perfected people, death leads to desired things that make worldly life seem trivial and frees them from trials and afflictions.
rows.anchor: ثم إنه لأهل الكمال وصلة إلى نيل المحاب التي تستحقر دونها الحياة الدنيوية وخلاص من أنواع المحن والبليات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Illness usually results from negligence in eating and drinking and from conflicting humors and elements; health requires their maintained union and a balance imposed by God's power.
rows.anchor: ولأن المرض في غالب الأمر إنما يحدث بتفريط من الإنسان في مطاعمه ومشاربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God causes death and then restores life in the hereafter.
rows.anchor: في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham mentions his hoped-for forgiveness in humility, teaching the community to avoid sin, be wary, seek pardon for failings, and ask forgiveness for possible minor lapses.
rows.anchor: ذكر ذلك هضما لنفسه وتعليما للأمة أن يجتنبوا المعاصي ويكونوا على حذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Identifying the sin with Abraham's three statements is weak, because they were indirect expressions rather than sins.
rows.anchor: ضعيف لأنها معاريض وليست خطايا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham asks for sound judgment in knowledge and action, preparing him for God's vicegerency and leadership of people.
rows.anchor: كما في العلم والعمل أستعد به لخلافة الحق ورياسة الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He asks to join the righteous through perfected action, counted among those whose complete righteousness is touched by neither major nor minor sin.
rows.anchor: ووفقني للكمال في العمل لأنتظم به في عداد الكاملين في الصلاح الذين لا يشوب صلاحهم كبير ذنب ولا صغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A tongue of truth means lasting worldly status and good renown through Judgment, explaining why every nation praises Abraham.
rows.anchor: جاها وحسن صيت في الدنيا يبقى أثره إلى يوم الدين، ولذلك ما من أمة إلا وهم محبون له مثنون عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it asks for a truthful descendant who renews Abraham's religion and calls people to his message: Muhammad.
rows.anchor: أو صادقا من ذريتي يجدد أصل ديني ويدعو الناس إلى ما كنت أدعوهم إليه وهو محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham asks to be an heir of the Garden of Bliss in the hereafter; the meaning of inheritance there was explained earlier.
rows.anchor: في الآخرة وقد مر معنى الوراثة فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His request that God forgive his father means to guide and enable him to believe.
rows.anchor: بالهداية والتوفيق للإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the prayer came after his father's death, Abraham may have thought he secretly believed while concealing faith from Nimrod, explaining his promise; alternatively, Abraham had not yet been barred from seeking forgiveness for unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وإن كان هذا الدعاء بعد موته فلعله كان لظنه أنه كان يخفي الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not disgrace me may mean do not rebuke me for failings, lower my rank, punish me, punish my father, or raise me among the misguided; disgrace may mean humiliation or shame.
rows.anchor: بمعاتبتي على ما فرطت، أو بنقص رتبتي عن رتبة بعض الوراث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in the resurrection phrase refers either to all servants, who are understood, or to the misguided.
rows.anchor: الضمير للعباد لأنهم معلومون أو ل { الضالين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sound heart is sincere, free of unbelief, sinful inclination, and other spiritual defects; wealth and children benefit only such a person.
rows.anchor: لا ينفعان أحدا إلا مخلصا سليم القلب عن الكفر وميل المعاصي وسائر آفاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, only the wealth and children of a sound-hearted person benefit: he spends wealth in good and guides his children to truth, virtue, and obedience so they may intercede for him.
rows.anchor: أو لا ينفعان إلا مال من هذا شأنه وبنوه حيث أنفق ماله في سبيل البر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception may derive from the implied idea that only one's own wealth benefits, or it may be disconnected: rather, the sound heart itself benefits its bearer.
rows.anchor: وقيل منقطع والمعنى لكن سلامة { من أتى الله بقلب سليم } تنفعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: We will see means we will find out through reflective looking; the wording intensifies the truthful-or-lying alternative and preserves the verse endings.
rows.anchor: أي أم كذبت والتغيير للمبالغة ومحافظة الفواصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon orders the hoopoe to deliver the letter and withdraw to a nearby concealed place to observe what the recipients say to one another.
rows.anchor: ثم تنح عنهم إلى مكان قريب تتوارى فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The letter is noble because of its content or sender, because it was sealed, or because its arrival was wondrous: the hoopoe entered her locked house through a window and dropped it on her neck while she reclined unaware.
rows.anchor: لكرم مضمونه أو مرسله، أو لأنه كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration that the letter is from Solomon resumes as though someone asked who sent it and what it says; it can refer to the letter or its heading, then to the text or its content.
rows.anchor: استئناف كأنه قيل لها ممن هو وما هو فقالت إنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternate reading with fatḥa on inna makes the phrase an apposition to كتاب or explains why it is noble.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بالفتح على الإبدال من { كتاب }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The initial ألا can be explanatory or infinitival as the predicate of an omitted subject, or the phrase can be an apposition to the letter.
rows.anchor: أن مفسرة أو مصدرية فتكون بصلتها خبر محذوف أي هو أو المقصود أن لا تعلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Coming to Solomon as Muslims means coming as believers or submitting in obedience.
rows.anchor: مؤمنين أو منقادين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The letter is concise but complete: the basmala explicitly or implicitly indicates God's existence and attributes, forbids arrogance as the root of vices, and commands Islam as the union of virtues.
rows.anchor: وهذا كلام في غاية الوجازة مع كمال الدلالة على المقصود، لاشتماله على البسملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request is not blind submission before proof: the circumstance in which the letter was delivered is itself powerful evidence of Solomon's message.
rows.anchor: وليس الأمر فيه بالانقياد قبل إقامة الحجة على رسالته حتى يكون استدعاء للتقليد فإن إلقاء الكتاب إليها على تلك الحالة من أعظم الدلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The queen asks her council to advise her about her current affair and tell her what they think best.
rows.anchor: أجيبوني في أمري الفتي واذكروا ما تستصوبون فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She says she does not decide an affair without the council present, appealing to their sympathy to gain their support for the response.
rows.anchor: إلا بمحضركم استعطفتهم بذلك ليمالئوها على الإجابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After explaining the beginning, end, and resurrection, the Prophet is told to declare that he is commanded to worship the Lord of this sacred town, signaling the mission is complete and only worship remains.
rows.anchor: أمر الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم بأن يقول لهم ذلك بعدما بين المبدأ والمعاد وشرح أحوال القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Mecca this town honors and magnifies it.
rows.anchor: في عبادة ربه، وتخصيص مكة بهذه الإضافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative pronoun is also read in the feminine form التي.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «التي حرمها»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything belongs to God by creation and ownership; Muslims means those compliant with Islam or steadfast in its religion.
rows.anchor: وأمرت أن أكون من المسلمين } المنقادين أو الثابتين على ملة الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reciting the Qur'an can mean persevering in recitation to uncover its realities gradually, or following it; alternate readings include واتل عليهم and وأن أتل.
rows.anchor: وأن أواظب على تلاوته لتنكشف لي حقائقه في تلاوته شيئا فشيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guided person follows the Prophet and benefits himself; the one who strays by opposing him bears the loss, since the Messenger only warns and has delivered the message.
rows.anchor: فلا علي من وبال ضلاله شيء إذ ما على الرسول إلا البلاغ وقد بلغت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praise God for the blessing of prophethood, or for teaching the Prophet and enabling him to act on what he learned.
rows.anchor: على نعمة النبوة أو على ما علمني ووفقني للعمل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will show signs of power in this world, such as Badr and the Beast of the Earth, or in the hereafter.
rows.anchor: القاهرة في الدنيا كوقعة بدر وخروج دابة الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will recognize the signs as God's only when recognition can no longer benefit them; delayed punishment does not mean God is unaware of their actions.
rows.anchor: فلا تحسبوا أن تأخير عذابكم لغفلته عن أعمالكم

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: They read the final verb with yāʾ rather than tāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي بالياء

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises ten good deeds per person who believed or disbelieved in Solomon, Hud, Salih, Abraham, and Shuayb; the reciter rises from the grave proclaiming there is no god but God. The source states no grading.
rows.anchor:
عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
" من قرأ سورة طس كان له من الأجر عشر حسنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The city is Egypt, reached from Pharaoh's palace; other identifications given are Manf, Hāʾīn, or Ain Shams in its vicinity.
rows.anchor: ودخل مصر آتيا من قصر فرعون وقيل منف أو حائين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time was one when entering was unusual and unexpected; views identify it as the midday nap or between the evening prayers.
rows.anchor: في وقت لا يعتاد دخولها ولا يتوقعونه فيه، قيل كان وقت القيلولة وقيل بين العشاءين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelite belonged to Moses' religious community, while the Copt opposed it; the labels are from the narrative's perspective.
rows.anchor: أحدهما ممن شايعه على دينه وهم بنو إسرائيل والآخر من مخالفيه وهم القبط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelite asked Moses to help against the Copt, which explains using على with the verb; another reading is استعانه.
rows.anchor: فسأله أن يغيثه بالإعانة ولذلك عدى ب { على } وقرىء «استعانه»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses struck the Copt with the fist of his hand; another reading means he struck his chest.
rows.anchor: فضرب القبطي بجمع كفه، وقرىء فلكزه أي فضرب به صدره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To finish him means to end his life, as in the verse about completing a matter.
rows.anchor: فقتله وأصله فأنهى حياته من قوله وقضينا إليه ذلك الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the killing Satan's work may mean Moses had no command to kill unbelievers or that he had been safe among them and should not have assassinated them; it does not undermine his protection from sin because it was an error, and prophets magnify small lapses.
rows.anchor: لأنه لم يؤمر بقتل الكفار أو لأنه كان مأمونا فيهم فلم يكن له اغتيالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan is plainly hostile and misleading.
rows.anchor: { إنه عدو مضل مبين } ظاهر العداوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses says he wronged himself by killing the man and asks forgiveness for his sin; God forgives him in response to his plea and is forgiving and merciful to His servants.
rows.anchor: بقتله. { فاغفر لى } ذنبي. { فغفر له } لاستغفاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause may be an oath with an omitted answer: by God's favor of forgiveness and more, Moses swears to repent and never support criminals.
rows.anchor: قسم محذوف الجواب أي أقسم بإنعامك علي بالمغفرة وغيرها لأتوبن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is an appeal for protection: by God's favor, keep Moses from aiding anyone whose assistance would lead to crime.
rows.anchor: أو استعطاف أي بحق إنعامك على أعصمني فلن أكون معينا لمن أدت معاونته إلى جرم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses did not qualify his promise, so he was tested by a similar event again.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما: أنه لم يستثن فابتلي به مرة أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation invokes the strength God bestowed: Moses will use it to aid God's allies, not support His enemies.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه بما أنعمت علي من القوة أعين أولياءك فلن أستعملها في مظاهرة أعدائك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses remained fearful and watchful in the city, anticipating retaliation.
rows.anchor: يترقب الاستقادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man who sought help from Moses the previous day cries out for aid; استصرخه derives from صراخ.
rows.anchor: يستغيثه مشتق من الصراخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses calls him an obvious troublemaker because he caused one man's death and is now fighting another.
rows.anchor: بين الغواية لأنك تسببت لقتل رجل وتقاتل آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone deserves worship; none but Him is worthy of it.
rows.anchor: المستحق للعبادة. { لا إله إلا هو } لا أحد يستحقها إلا هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All praise belongs to Him because He grants every immediate and ultimate favor; believers praise Him in the next life as in this life, rejoicing in His favor and delighting in praise.
rows.anchor: لأنه المولى للنعم كلها عاجلها وآجلها يحمده المؤمنون في الآخرة كما حمدوه في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's judgment is an effective decree over everything, and return to Him occurs through resurrection.
rows.anchor: القضاء النافذ في كل شيء. { وإليه ترجعون } بالنشور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sar-mad denotes unceasing night, from the root of following one thing continuously; the m is an addition, as in دلامص.
rows.anchor: دائما من السرد وهو المتابعة والميم مزيدة كميم دلامص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Permanent night would last until resurrection either with the sun below the earth or moving around the hidden horizon.
rows.anchor: بإسكان الشمس تحت الأرض أو تحريكها حول الأفق الغائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expected wording is هل إله; using من reflects the opponents' claim that other gods exist.
rows.anchor: كان حقه هل إله فذكر ب { من } على زعمهم أن غيره آلهة

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir reads the word for light with two hamzas.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن كثير «بضئاء» بهمزتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Will you not hear means hear through reflection and insight.
rows.anchor: سماع تدبر واستبصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day the torment covers them can be an adverb of محيطة or of an implied predicate such as a description of what happened.
rows.anchor: ظرف { لمحيطة } أو مقدرة مثل كان كيت وكيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The torment comes from above and beneath their feet, meaning from every direction.
rows.anchor: من جميع جوانبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker may be God or some angels acting by God's command; Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, and the Basran readers recite the verb in first-person plural.
rows.anchor: الله أو بعض ملائكته بأمره لقراءة ابن كثير وابن عامر والبصريين بالنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are told to taste the recompense for their own deeds.
rows.anchor: أي جزاءه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers unable to worship openly or practice their religion in a town should migrate to a place where they can worship God alone.
rows.anchor: إذا لم يتسهل لكم العبادة في بلدة ولم يتيسر لكم إظهار دينكم فهاجروا إلى حيث يتمشى لكم ذلك

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says that one who flees for faith from one land to another, even by a span, merits Paradise and companionship with Abraham and Muhammad; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor:
وعنه عليه الصلاة والسلام:
" من فر بدينه من أرض إلى أرض ولو كان شبرا استوجب الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ف answers an omitted condition: if believers cannot worship sincerely in one land, they should worship sincerely elsewhere.
rows.anchor: الفاء جواب شرط محذوف إذ المعنى إن أرضي واسعة إن لم تخلصوا العبادة لي في أرض فأخلصوها في غيرها
